_about: The study's register. Each rule is scored only on trades entered AFTER after_ts (out of sample); the study adds rules here and never edits an existing one's filter or after_ts. filter ops: < <= > >= == != on columns of data/abcd.csv; exit is the paper column to score (x_flow4 runner, x_h5 5-min, x_h3 3-min, x_h15, x_h5f14, x_t15s40).

strategies.note: sell at 3 minutes instead of 5 (from 84 post-fix trades: +10.1% vs +5.0%)
fewer than 65 wallets in the trigger minute (from 49 live coins: 72% win vs 38%)
one buyer took more than 10% of the trigger minute's buying (from 49 live coins: 75% win vs 36%)

study's own: A coins whose launch bundle was at most 3 wallets, runner exit. From 100 passed A trades: n33 +18.4% net, 76-85% win, 12% stopped vs n67 -9.0% net, 37-40% win; holds at the 5-s fill price (+13.9%), in 10 of 13 hours, and on D's coins (n27 +13.2% vs n53 -8.7%, mostly the same mints). Hypothesis until 40 out-of-sample trades.

study's own LAUNCH-TIME rule (score by hand from launches.csv, create_ts > after_ts): a tier-1 bundled launch (bundle 40-79% of supply, median dev buy 4.9 SOL, ~25 an hour), bought at the +4 s price (median MC $32K), sold at 5 min. 604 launches in 24 h: 5-min multiple median 1.24 on the 86% still trading, 44% above the 10% cost, 28% reached 5x and 16% 10x by 5 min, 55% graduated; positive in all six 4-hour blocks. The website's bundled-70%+ skip and S4's clean-launch premise point the other way. Not yet a book: needs the executor to see whether the +4 s price is obtainable (bundle sells into the buy) — judge on the next 24 h of launches first.

the owner's E trigger ($100K traded in 5 min, MC under $100K) sold at 5 minutes: the best E exit so far, +8.8% net on 31 passed trades (runner +5.3%, 1.5x/-40% -0.1%); 31 trades is too few to mean anything.

study's own LAUNCH-TIME rule, scored by hand from launches.csv (create_ts > after_ts; the study.mjs table cannot score it). One operator's signature: the create block buys 37-41% of supply over exactly 10 wallets with 22-27 SOL, the creator's own buy is under 0.2 SOL, no socials. 14 launches in 24 h (18 Oct 16:21 to 19 Oct 10:23 UTC): all 14 peaked >= $200K and graduated; from the +4 s price (median MC $11K) the 60-s mark was 15-45x (median 19.5x, fill 13/14), the 5-min mark 16-24x on the 9 with a mark. Base rate for an ordinary launch: 0.12% reach $200K. Replaces F2 (verdict below): F2's lift was a different factory that buys the whole curve in one wallet (bundle 79.3%, 85 SOL) and cannot be bought at +4 s; S8's buyable tier-1 coins lose. Open questions: whether the +4 s price exists for an outside buyer (the 10 wallets may front-run the curve themselves), and whether the operator keeps launching. Hypothesis until 40 launches; judge from 20 given the base rate.

study's own: the G book's coins (A's trigger, skipped by the website for 150-500 wallets) sold at 5 minutes instead of the runner. Score by hand from A rows with skip_why = N wallets (the study.mjs table scores on passed rows and will show 0). Evidence: 36 such trades since the price fix, 5-min sell +20.5% net (win 64%) and 1.5x/-40% +5.9%, against the runner -1.4% and G's 7 shadow runner legs -0.327 SOL (4 stops). At 13:28 it was +35.9% on 26, so the last 10 were about -20%: the edge is fading, which is why it is registered rather than recommended. Hypothesis until 40 out-of-sample trades.

A5 itself (the owner's rule, book A5 / p5c5 from 19 Oct 19:10 UTC): A's coin bought 5 s after the trigger only if the price is still >= 1.02x, runner exit. PRICED FROM THE 5-s PRICE: score by hand as x_flow4 / fs5_x (the study.mjs table prices it at the trigger price and will overstate it by ~15 points). In sample on the rows the owner saw (to 16:05 UTC): 51 trades +4.4% net at real costs, win 63%, stopped 25% vs A -1.8%/39%. On the 10 rows from 16:05 to 19:10 UTC: -13.7%. Hypothesis until 40 out-of-sample trades; also score the real A5 rows/legs (book A5) side by side.

study's own: a stricter, later confirm than A5 — A's coin bought 10 s after the trigger only if the price is still >= 1.05x, runner exit. PRICED FROM THE 10-s PRICE: score by hand as x_flow4 / fs10_x. From 152 passed A trades: 56 qualify, +8.3% net at real costs, win 68%, stopped 12% (A: 39%); +8.4% on the 45 to 16:05 UTC and +7.7% on the 11 after; positive in 12 of 20 hours. The one re-priced confirm rule out of 75 tried (2-/5-/10-s price x 1.02-1.25 x 3 exits x 13 books) that is positive in both halves — the selection risk is real. Needs the executor to buy at the 10-s price, which the tracker only sees when its feed lag is under a second (19:39 UTC it was 21 s). Hypothesis until 40 out-of-sample trades.

study's own: S3 (copycat) only when the buy is at least 1 s after the launch (sn_delay_s >= 1), sold at 5 min, curve costs. From 91 closed S3 rows: 62 qualify, +13.9% net, win 37%, stopped 26%; +5.3% on the first half and +22.5% on the 31 since 16:05 UTC; the 29 same-second buys are -25.0% (win 14%). S3's shadow legs (34 since 16:15 UTC, +0.174 SOL, entry gap +1.4%) say the paper price is obtainable. Suspicion to check: the same-second rows may be priced at the create trade, which an outsider cannot get. Found among 4,821 rule tests; hypothesis until 40 out-of-sample trades.
